summary: Documented M4-S01 (Business Hours for EMEA/US and the 24/7 Severity 1 calendar, plus holidays) after it reached `tested`. Re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md from plan.json; appended 5 decisions.md entries covering the checker-policy block on `Severity 1 24x7` and its closure at the skill (D-M4S01-01, the flywheel record), the 14-holiday seed placeholder and Q90's role-not-person owner gap (D-M4S01-02), the calendar's presently-unconsumed status pending a Severity 1 entitlement process (O-M4S01-01), the UNVERIFIED midnight-pair semantics (O-M4S01-02), and a check_rtm.py skill-depth signal on its per-calendar key derivation inside a Settings component (O-M4S01-03); wrote 4 workbook rows (CWB-AUT-013..014 in Section 6, CWB-OTHER-025..026 in Other Configuration); added 2 traceability rows (REQ-038 the three business-hours calendars, REQ-039 the holiday-maintenance runbook) plus 2 Requirement-id-derivation entries; ran check_rtm.py from the build dir (39 rows, 0 coverage gaps, 0 errors, 3 orphans found and explained by O-M4S01-03, matching O-M3S02-05/O-M3S04-03; exit 0 at both build and step scope); set the step to `documented`.
confidence_rationale: Every artefact produced a workbook row with a real source_req_id and a verification cell, and both new requirements have a traceability row (the HIGH conditions), but the check_rtm.py orphan WARN needed judgment rather than a mechanical read: the SETTINGS_ENTRIES per-calendar key derivation is a new checker behaviour this build had not seen before, and deciding it was a skill-depth signal rather than a row-naming error (recorded as O-M4S01-03) followed the same reasoning as two prior entries but required re-reading the checker's source to confirm the pattern actually matched.

process_observations.observation: The artefact under documentation is byte-for-byte identical between the blocked run and the built run — the checker-policy block was closed by scoping the rule at the skill, never by editing the settings file — so this documentation pass rests on one stable artefact rather than two versions to reconcile.

step-tester independently re-ran the declared checker command verbatim, from the build directory, and observed the same exit 0 the builder's own re-run recorded — two independent runs, same result, so the tested-status green is not resting on one agent's own say-so.
deploy-order.md is undeclared in M4-S01's outputs[], extending the same undeclared-artefact pattern (decisions.md O-M3S02-03) from every M3 step into M4.

Severity 1 24x7 is built and passes its checker, but no step in this build's current scope reads it by name — it is a metadata placeholder for a Severity 1 entitlement process that does not yet exist, and that gap is invisible to every exit code that touched this step.

The 14-holiday set in the deployed file is a seeded placeholder computed by the builder, not a source-grounded answer to which holidays Acme actually observes, and Q90's owner row names a role and a cadence but not a person.

check_rtm.py reports 3 orphans for this step's own component because its SETTINGS_ENTRIES derivation registers one key per businessHours calendar inside the file, alongside the container key the manifest and every other Settings row in this build actually names; 0 coverage gaps and 0 errors otherwise, at both build and step scope.

milestone-verifier should run once every M4 step is documented, because the checker-policy history, the unconsumed Severity 1 24x7 calendar, and the seeded holiday list are all cross-step or gate-level items rather than something one step's own tests settle.
process_observations.followup_reason: because the checker-policy history, the unconsumed calendar, and the seeded holiday list are all M4-gate items rather than settled by this step alone.

process_observations.observation: business-hours-and-holidays-configurator is the cross-step consumer map this skill's own template asks for, once M4-S02/M4-S03/M4-S04 are all built and the calendar's actual consumers (or lack of one for Severity 1 24x7) can be confirmed end to end.
process_observations.followup_reason: because it owns the cross-step consumer-map audit this skill's template calls for, which this step's own scope cannot complete alone.
